_comment: Hand-authored migration of verdicts EARNED IN THIS SESSION. Matched by quotation text fragment, never by line number. Evidence transfer only - no re-adjudication. Each entry cites where the verdict was earned.

entries.match: If you knew how perfect it all is
entries.notes: Documented fake-Buddha quote. Earliest trace 2001 Usenet, posted as 'Buddhist' not as the Buddha. Restoration lead: Longchenpa.

entries.match: If you knew how perfect it all is
entries.notes: Second occurrence of one saying. Rule with the family, not alone.

entries.match: When you realize how perfect everything is
entries.notes: THIRD occurrence, block form, different wording. Independently ruled in Stage 2 and reached the same Longchenpa ancestor. Linkage found only by the speaker sweep.
entries.evidence_location: QUOTATION_PROVENANCE_AUDIT.md (as L1939); linkage in STAGE4 speaker sweep

entries.match: Life can only be understood backwards
entries.translator_or_mediator: UNIDENTIFIED - rights depend on which English is printed (Dru 1938 vs Hong 1967-78)

entries.match: I don't have beliefs, I have experiences
entries.work: cf. BBC Face to Face (1959): 'I don't need to believe. I know.'
entries.notes: HOST-ALIGNED ALTERATION - clearest instance in the book. Jung's distinction is belief vs knowledge; the manuscript substitutes experience, and the host paragraph argues experience over belief. Restoring the authentic wording would not serve the host argument, which is the diagnostic.

entries.match: The mind is its own place
entries.notes: SPEAKER MISATTRIBUTION. Introduced as 'Milton aptly noted'. The section diagnoses the ego lost in cold logic - which is what Satan is doing. Correct attribution would strengthen the example.

entries.translator_or_mediator: Arthur Waley, The Way and Its Power (1934) - UNNAMED; 'usefulness' substituted for Waley's 'utility'
entries.notes: Longest quotation in the manuscript (~90 words) and its highest rights exposure - and it sat outside the census entirely.
Own source class. No published source, no bibliography obligation, no permissions clearance. Confirm consent before publication.

entries.match: Be in the world but not of it
entries.work: summarises John 17:14-16; the phrase does NOT appear at John 17:16
entries.internal_speaker: Jesus, praying - unnamed in the citation
entries.notes: False precision. 'The Christian admonition' is accurate; the chapter-and-verse citation is what makes it a false quotation. Removing the verse number makes the sentence MORE accurate.
entries.evidence_location: STAGE4 speaker sweep; STAGE2C-ii Part A

entries.work: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (c.1790), 'Proverbs of Hell'
entries.internal_speaker: the devil's voice in Blake's satirical frame
entries.bibliography_relationship: Blake present for a DIFFERENT work (doors of perception)
entries.notes: UNDER-ATTRIBUTED ('As it is said') plus lost speaker context. Two defects pointing in opposite directions. Fourth speaker specimen and the first found by under-attribution. | MATCH KEY UPDATED after the 4I REFRAME restored Blake's authentic wording. A similarity fallback was tried and REVERTED because it attached to the wrong record: failure to attach is safer than plausible attachment to the wrong semantic object.
No primary source. Several materially different variants circulate. The manuscript's own hedge 'is quoted as saying' was already signalling uncertainty.
